issue.title: [bug] SandboxAuditMiddleware blocks legitimate $(curl ...) command substitution, with no way to disable it

steps: Run this shell command and report its real output: code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://example.com --max-time 10); echo "$code"
expected: Capturing curl output is not rejected as execution of downloaded code; an egress error, if any, is reported separately.
defect: SandboxAuditMiddleware classifies the output-capturing $(curl ...) expression as a blocked high-risk command before execution.
Root cause: The command-substitution pattern matches curl regardless of the substitution position. #4623 distinguishes capturing output from executing downloaded content.

_meta.notes: The command is from the issue, with --max-time 10 to bound network waiting. Successful network access is not a precondition: only the pre-execution audit refusal is the target.
_meta.version_installation_validation: not_executed; historical launch and dependency compatibility must be checked before running
_meta.historical_entry_check: native embedded LangGraph client; ACP not required
